speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing sudden-onset lower back pain radiating down your leg. To begin our evaluation, on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is this pain, and does it worsen with coughing or sneezing?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pain sounds like sciatica. Did you hear a "pop" or "snap" at the moment it started, and do you have any numbness or weakness in your leg or foot? REQUEST TEST: Neurological_Exam

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Sensation: Intact to light touch and pin-prick throughout the leg and foot. Motor_Function: No significant weakness noted. Reflexes: Normal ankle and knee reflexes.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mention of iron deficiency anemia seems unrelated to your sharp pain radiating down your leg; please ignore that previous advice. Did the pain begin while you were lifting a heavy weight or twisting your back, and is the pain worse when you straighten your leg or cough? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Lumbar_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Lumbar_Spine: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: L5-S1 Disc Herniation. The MRI results confirming a disc herniation at L5-S1 impinging on the nerve root, combined with your history of sudden onset pain during exercise and radiation to the foot, are definitive for this diagnosis.
